mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (indicating monetary easing) compresses discount rates for equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.1% over the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month rise in the unemployment rate exceeding 0.2 percentage points signals economic deterioration, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Unemployment rate increased from 4.4% to 4.7% between July and October 2007
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and real personal consumption expenditures signal a broad-based demand contraction, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Housing market collapse and slowing consumption in 2007
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline by at least 0.5% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: In a high inflation regime (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), a decline in industrial production signals an impending economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Inflation was moderate but rising in 2007
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO declines by at least 0.5% in the prior month and CPIAUCSL > 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in non-farm payrolls indicates a strengthening labor market, supporting corporate earnings and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Payrolls increased by 100,000 in the prior month (from 137.165 million to 138.265 million)
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS increases by at least 100,000 in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: When year-over-year CPI inflation exceeds 3.0%, it triggers expectations of tighter monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:CPI index at 207.738 implies about 2.7% yoy growth (but threshold set at 3.0%)
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL yoy > 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate and CPI inflation signal a monetary tightening cycle, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Federal funds rate rising and inflation accelerating in 2007
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.25% and CPIAUCSL yoy rises by at least 0.5% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: In a slow GDP growth regime (GDPC1 growth < 2.0% annualized), a decline in housing starts signals further housing sector deterioration, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Q2 2007 GDP growth was 2.0% (annualized) and housing starts were declining
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when HOUST declines by at least 1.0% in the prior month and GDPC1 growth < 2.0% annualized.
